stories.title: Ethereum sees biggest exchange withdrawal in four months as October ETF losses top $1 billion
stories.summary: Ethereum recorded its largest exchange withdrawal in four months. The move comes as Ethereum ETFs have lost more than $1 billion in October.
stories.whyItMatters: Large exchange withdrawals and ETF outflows both signal how institutions and holders feel about ETH right now.
whatToWatch: Whether ETF outflows continue through the rest of October
Whether exchange withdrawals keep accelerating
questions: What is driving the outflows: broad market conditions or ETH-specific concerns?
Will the withdrawal trend reverse or continue?

stories.title: Bitcoin Core speeds up security fixes as 44% of nodes run unsupported versions
stories.summary: Bitcoin Core developers are moving faster to ship security fixes. A survey found 44% of nodes on the network run software versions that no longer get support.
stories.whyItMatters: Outdated node software leaves gaps that could threaten the security of the whole Bitcoin network.
whatToWatch: The next Bitcoin Core release and its adoption rate
Whether node operators upgrade in response
questions: What specifically prompted the faster fix schedule?
Will operators on unsupported versions upgrade in time?

stories.title: Ethereum staking yield now trails cash rates, yet investors keep staking
stories.summary: Ethereum staking yields have fallen below returns available from cash-like instruments. Despite this, investors continue to stake ETH in large numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap shows staking demand is not driven by yield alone, which matters for anyone modeling ETH supply and investor behavior.
whatToWatch: Further moves in staking yield versus cash rates
Staking inflow and outflow trends
questions: Why are investors staking despite the lower relative yield?
Does this reflect long-term conviction or just liquid-staking convenience?

sources.title: Ethereum staking yield is losing to cash rates, so why are investors still lining up?

stories.title: Senator probes Tether's reported $6 million payments to ex-White House crypto adviser's firm
stories.summary: A U.S. senator is probing Tether over reported payments of $6 million to a firm tied to a former White House crypto adviser.
stories.whyItMatters: The inquiry raises conflict-of-interest questions about ties between a major stablecoin issuer and crypto policymaking.
whatToWatch: The senator's formal findings or document requests
Tether's response to the inquiry
questions: What were the payments for?
Is there an actual conflict of interest with crypto policy?

stories.title: Wall Street's $359 billion-a-day repo market finds a use for blockchain
stories.summary: The repo market, which handles roughly $359 billion in transactions daily, has reportedly begun using blockchain technology for part of its operations.
stories.whyItMatters: Adoption of blockchain infrastructure in core bond-market plumbing would mark a notable step for institutional use of the technology.
whatToWatch: Further details on the rollout and which institutions are involved
Signs of wider adoption across the repo market
questions: Which blockchain platform or technology is being used?
Which banks or firms are participating?

stories.title: JUST ecosystem says it upgraded JST buyback-and-burn with GasFree revenue and a $20.34M surplus
stories.summary: The JUST ecosystem says it has upgraded its JST buyback-and-burn program, adding GasFree service revenue and injecting a reported $20.34 million surplus.

Any independent confirmation of the surplus figure

Is GasFree revenue sustainable going forward?

stories.title: New York seeks $1.3 billion from NovaTech as 11,000 victims face delayed recovery
stories.summary: New York regulators are seeking $1.3 billion from NovaTech in a case tied to roughly 11,000 alleged victims, who now face delays in recovering funds.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows the scale of ongoing enforcement against crypto investment schemes and the slow path victims face toward restitution.
whatToWatch: Progress of the recovery and restitution process
Any court rulings or deadlines in the case
questions: What was NovaTech's alleged scheme?
Why are victims facing delays in recovery?

stories.title: New OCC rule resets stablecoin redemption requirements, forcing bank changes
stories.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has issued a new rule changing how stablecoin redemptions must work, requiring banks to adjust their processes.
stories.whyItMatters: Redemption rules are a core part of stablecoin stability, so a federal banking regulator's changes affect issuers and the banks that support them.
whatToWatch: Bank compliance timelines for the new rule
How stablecoin issuers respond
questions: Which banks or issuers face the biggest changes?
What is the implementation deadline?

stories.title: HSBC's RedCoin reaches 3.3 million users, but one restriction limits access
stories.summary: HSBC's RedCoin is now available to about 3.3 million users. A strict restriction, not fully detailed in initial reporting, still limits how they can use it.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank pushing a crypto-linked product to millions of users signals growing mainstream interest, even with limits attached.
whatToWatch: Whether HSBC eases or lifts the restriction
Actual usage numbers among the eligible 3.3 million
questions: What exactly is RedCoin?
What is the specific rule blocking full use?

stories.title: Aave changes USDT borrowing rules, and loan costs jump
stories.summary: Aave has changed its rules for borrowing USDT on its lending protocol. Borrowing costs rose suddenly as a result.
stories.whyItMatters: Rate changes on a major DeFi lending protocol can squeeze leveraged borrowers and shift liquidity across the sector.
whatToWatch: Whether borrowing rates stabilize or keep rising
Whether users shift borrowing to other protocols
questions: What prompted the rule change?
How large is the rate increase, and who is most affected?
